status_summary: The FCC has acted on one media ownership rule, the 39 percent national television ownership cap, but the order is not shown to be in effect. On 2026-08-06 the Commission voted 2-1 to repeal the cap in favor of case-by-case review of transactions, through Report and Order FCC 26-53 in MB Docket 17-318; the FCC's own release gives no effective date, and a stay petition filed with the FCC on 2026-10-02 by ten state and regional cable associations says the order takes effect 60 days after Federal Register publication. As of 2026-10-23 a Federal Register search on the docket found no publication of the order, and no court petition was found. On the wider rules review, the FCC's Delete, Delete, Delete proceeding has published a series of rules removing outdated regulations since 2025-08-04, including on 2026-06-22 and 2026-09-10; no action on other media ownership rules was found.

timeline.event: The Media Bureau publishes a request for updated comment on whether to change, keep or eliminate the 39 percent national audience reach cap and the UHF discount (MB Docket 17-318).

The FCC publishes the first final rules in its Delete, Delete, Delete proceeding, removing outdated, obsolete and unnecessary regulations and changing delegated authority for deletions exempt from notice and comment; further deletion rules follow, including on 2025-08-20, 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-14 (Federal Register lists 44 FCC documents mentioning the proceeding since 2025-01-20).
The FCC publishes a rule titled Deletion of Obsolete Regulations, which removes outdated rules, including some in the broadcast part of its regulations.

An FCC press release announces an order to replace the 39 percent national television ownership cap with case-by-case review, weighing localism, viewpoint diversity and competition where relevant, with a vote set for 2026-08-06.
A Federal Register Sunshine Act notice lists a Report and Order amending the National Television Multiple Ownership Rule (47 CFR 73.3555(e), MB Docket 17-318) for the 2026-08-06 meeting.

The FCC adopts, by a 2-1 vote (Chairman Carr and Commissioner Trusty in favor, Commissioner Gomez dissenting), Report and Order FCC 26-53 in MB Docket 17-318 repealing the 39 percent national television multiple ownership rule and replacing it with case-by-case review of transactions; the FCC's news release calls it the first change to the rule in over 20 years and states no effective date, and Commissioner Gomez's dissent argues that the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2004 fixed the cap in statute so only Congress can change it.

The FCC publishes a final rule in its Delete, Delete, Delete proceeding (FCC 26-56, GN Docket 25-133) removing the ASCII format requirement and definition for text-telephone relay services, effective 2026-10-13.

title: Eliminate dated FCC media ownership rules and review FCC rules for repeal
uncertainties: The FCC news release of 2026-08-06 confirms the action, vote, order number, docket and the absence of an effective date; the Commissioner Gomez statement is a dissent saying only Congress can raise or remove the cap. The adopted Report and Order text itself was not read, so the case-by-case test, any treatment of the UHF discount and the effective-date clause are unverified. The stay petition (read in a copy hosted by a trade outlet) is dated 2026-10-02, cites 5 U.S.C. 705, asks the FCC to rule by the publication date and states that the full order was released on 2026-10-01; that release date rests on the petition alone and is not entered as an event. The petition is a private filing in the FCC docket, and trade reports of the vote and of the petition (NewscastStudio, Light Reading) are kept as sources rather than events; Free Press's stated plan to appeal was reported by Axios. A Federal Register API search on docket 17-318 after 2026-08-06 returned no documents, and a search of FCC rules from 2026-08-07 to 2026-10-19 found no ownership rule, but the index may lag. The petition also cites a pending D.C. Circuit case on a separate Media Bureau merger order and a California federal merger case; they concern a transaction, not the cap repeal, and were not reviewed. A 2026-09-03 correction in the Delete, Delete, Delete series and several broadcast channel allotment rules were seen but not treated as events. No Federal Register document on local ownership rules or the top-four prohibition was found. The Mandate's universal service point on p.857 is not assessed here.
